subject: ventures/slo-burn-rate-alerts
professional: a senior SRE who writes Prometheus alerting rules for SLOs (multiwindow, multi-burn-rate alerts per the Google SRE Workbook, Sloth/Pyrra-style generators); first checks: do the burn rates and windows match the Workbook table, are the error-budget and threshold numbers right, is the generated PromQL valid and does the alert require BOTH windows, does each alert actually fire at the predicted time on synthetic traffic, are thresholds that can never fire (or that fire while the SLO is met) caught, and are the recording rules a ratio of sums

evidence.correctness: Recomputed against the Google SRE Workbook, 'Alerting on SLOs' (multiwindow multi-burn-rate table and its example rule config: 14.4x 1h/5m for 2%, 6x 6h/30m for 5%, 3x 1d/2h and 1x 3d/6h for 10%, 30-day window) and by hand. `node cli.mjs plan --slo 99.9 --rps 40`: burns 14.4/6/3/1, thresholds 1.44%/0.600%/0.300%/0.100%, budget 43m 12s (30x24x60x0.001 = 43.2 min), week 10m 5s (604.8 s), year 8h 45m 36s (31,536 s): all match. `plan --slo 99.95 --period 28`: 13.44x (0.02x672h/1h), 0.672%, 20m 10s (1,209.6 s): match. Detection times checked with my own per-second simulation of the two-window ratio after a 3-day healthy period (scratchpad slo/sim.mjs, does not import engine.mjs): total outage 52/130/260/260 s vs engine 51.84/129.6/259.2/259.2; 2% errors 2,593 s vs 2,592 (43.2 min); 1% errors: 1h page never, 6h page 12,961 s vs 12,960: all agree. Unreachable lint: 93% SLO gives 14.4x0.07 = 1.008, flagged ERROR, exit 1. Generated PromQL read against the Workbook example and Prometheus rule syntax: ratio-of-sums recording rules, `rec1h{slo="api"} > (14.4 * 0.001) and rec5m{slo="api"} > (14.4 * 0.001)`, valid; running promtool check/test rules was refused by this sandbox, so validity is by reading only. Not 4: for periods under 30 days burn rates fall below 1 unflagged (period 1 day pages at 0.48x, i.e. while the SLO is met) and `rules` writes a never-firing alert at exit 0.
evidence.completeness: Every README/page feature works end to end: `plan` text and --json, exit codes (0 ok, 1 on unreachable or warn with --fail-on warn, 2 on bad input: `--slo 100`, `-5`, `0`, `''`, `--period 0/-3`, `--rps -1` all exit 2), `rules` emits the stated 7 recording rules (5m,30m,1h,2h,6h,1d,3d) and 4 alerts (2 page, 2 ticket), lint for unreachable/low-traffic/extreme-target, browser page renders budget, policy, findings, rules, copy and download; how-to page and llms.txt present; live page https://marisstella.app/slo-burn-rate-alerts/ returns 200. No stubs or TODOs.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 34 tests, 34 pass, 127 ms. Tests pin the main numbers (14.4/6/3/1, 43m 12s, 51.84 s, 13.44). Seeded 8 mutants with quality_mutate.py: 3 caught (Math.max->min in detectionTime, long->short window in detectionTime, toFixed(3)->toFixed(1) on burn), 5 survived: `and` -> `or` between the long and short windows in the generated alert (the core of the multiwindow method), reachable `< 1` -> `<= 1`, low-traffic `< 1` -> `< 0.5`, extreme-target `1e-6` -> `1e-9`, per-year 365 -> 360 days. No test runs the rules through promtool or any PromQL parser, and no test covers the page's render() path.
evidence.craft: Read engine.mjs (183 lines), cli.mjs (88), usage.mjs, index.html script, all four test files. One shared pure engine for CLI and page, input validation, JSON-quoted YAML strings: clean. Defects found by running the page in Playwright: entering a blank, 0 or -5 SLO, or a 0/-7 period after a good run shows the error in a small status line but leaves the previous 99.9% report, policy table and rules file visible and copyable/downloadable (index.html:133 returns without hiding #report-card or clearing lastRules); a negative rps is silently ignored on the page (CLI rejects it); the policy table overflows at 375 px (scrollWidth 427); selectors are not syntax-checked (`--errors 'e[5m]' --total 't)'` emits `rate(e[5m][5m])` and `rate(t)[5m])` at exit 0); the short-period lint text is muddled; the CLI prints 'error ratio > 101%' while the lint says 100.8%.
evidence.claims: Checked 9 claims. Backed: downtime budget, Workbook thresholds, outage detection times (simulation), unreachable and low-traffic lint, '7 recording rules and 4 alerts', exit codes, 'nothing is uploaded' (Playwright saw only same-origin index.html, engine.mjs, usage.mjs requests; no fetch/beacon in source), DNT/GPC honoured (usage.mjs:34), no-warranty disclaimer on both pages, served llms.txt carries marisstella.app URLs (served-copy.mjs: no placeholder left). Not backed: (1) the FAQ question 'Why does my 99% or 90% SLO never alert?' (index.html:12 FAQPage schema and :103): at 99% the thresholds are 14.4%/6%/3%/1%, all reachable, and `plan --slo 99` reports 0 errors; (2) the headline promise of 'alert rules that actually fire' while `rules --slo 90` exits 0 and writes the 1h alert whose threshold is 144%, with no comment in the file.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job of an engineer defining a first availability SLO: typed 99.9/30 and the page gave the budget, thresholds, detection times and a rules file whose alert logic my independent simulation fires at the predicted times. For a 28/30-day ratio SLI on counters the file is a usable starting point after promtool. Gaps a senior SRE hits: latency SLIs cannot be expressed (the selector is wrapped in rate(), so 'total minus le bucket' is impossible); windows and budget fractions are fixed although the lint tells the user to 'use a longer long-window or a smaller budget fraction'; no error-budget-remaining recording rule or promtool unit-test file as Sloth/Pyrra provide; short periods produce sub-1x pages without a warning.
evidence.domain: Matches the Workbook: the four (fraction, long, short) rows of its example config, short window = long/12, threshold = burn x (1 - SLO), both windows ANDed, recording rules as sum(rate(errors))/sum(rate(total)), and its low-traffic caveat. Departures: burn = fraction x period / window is applied to any period 1-366 days, so below 30 days the 3d ticket drops under 1x (28 d 0.933, 7 d 0.233), below 10 days the 1d ticket does, below 5 days the 6h page does and below 2.08 days the 1h page does (period 1 day: 0.48x) - an alert under 1x fires while the service is meeting its SLO, and lint flags none of this (only an 'info' line for periods under 7 days, nothing at 7). Detection times ignore scrape/evaluation interval and rate()'s two-sample minimum (it reports 0s and 2s detections). Separate alerts per row instead of the Workbook's or-combined page/ticket rules is an acceptable variant.

defects.what: Burn rates below 1 are generated and not flagged: burn = fraction x period / window is applied to any period, so the 3d ticket is under 1x below 30 days, the 1d ticket below 10, the 6h page below 5 and the 1h page below 2.08 days (period 1: pages at 0.48x and 0.2x). An alert under 1x fires while the service meets its SLO. Lint gives only an INFO line for periods under 7 days (with muddled wording) and nothing at 7 days (tickets at 0.7x and 0.233x)

`rules` for an SLO with an unreachable threshold exits 0 and writes the never-firing alert (e.g. 90%: 1h page at 144%) with no comment, against the product's 'alert rules that actually fire' promise; only `plan` exits 1

Tests would not catch the core multiwindow bug: changing `and` to `or` between the long and short windows in the generated alert survives, as do the reachable boundary (< 1 -> <= 1), the low-traffic and extreme-target thresholds and the per-year length (5 of 8 mutants); no test parses the PromQL or runs promtool, and the page's render() is untested
Page leaves the previous report and rules file visible and copyable when the SLO or period is changed to blank, 0 or negative: only a small status line shows the error
FAQ (visible and FAQPage schema) asks 'Why does my 99% or 90% SLO never alert?'; at 99% every threshold is reachable (14.4%/6%/3%/1%) and the tool reports 0 errors
Page silently ignores a negative requests/sec value; the CLI rejects it with exit 2
Selectors are not syntax-checked: `--errors 'e[5m]' --total 't)'` emits `rate(e[5m][5m])` and `rate(t)[5m])` at exit 0 (mitigated by the promtool advice)

Latency SLIs cannot be expressed (the selector is wrapped in rate(), so total minus a histogram bucket is impossible) and windows/fractions are fixed although the unreachable lint tells the user to use a longer long-window or smaller budget fraction
Detection time ignores scrape/evaluation interval and rate()'s two-sample minimum, so it reports 0s or 2s detections Prometheus cannot achieve; a 99.99999% SLO shows '0s' budget for 0.26 s
Policy table overflows a 375 px viewport (scrollWidth 427)

verdict: A small, clean SLO alert generator whose arithmetic is right where it matters: burn rates, thresholds and windows match the SRE Workbook's multiwindow table, budgets and the 28-day variant recompute by hand, and detection times agree with an independent per-second simulation to the second. The generated rules are valid PromQL by reading (promtool could not be run here) and follow the Workbook's ratio-of-sums form. It misses the bar on claims and verification: the FAQ says a 99% SLO never alerts (it does), `rules` writes a never-firing alert at exit 0 despite the 'rules that actually fire' promise, and 5 of 8 seeded bugs survive the tests, including swapping the two-window `and` for `or`. Short periods yield sub-1x pages and tickets that fire while the SLO is met, unflagged, and the page keeps a stale report and rules after blank, zero or negative input. Finished for what it claims, not yet at senior-SRE sign-off.
